title: Radio transmitter (FM stereo + RDS, NFM, AM, SSB, CW, digital, pictures, AES67)
summary: A radio station on one pin, made inside the FPGA: FM stereo with your station name and text on the radio's display (RDS), NFM, AM, USB, LSB and DSB, Morse code, RTTY and PSK31, pictures (SSTV), songs from WAV files and live sound from the network (AES67).
wiring: a short wire, 10 to 20 cm, as the antenna
a few meters of range in a room; the self-test needs nothing
J9 pin 11 through a 1 kohm resistor
an SDR input (RTL-SDR) through a 30 to 40 dB attenuator
never the pin straight into an SDR: the resistor and the attenuator protect it and keep the signal off the air
the ground (outer conductor) of the SDR cable
parts: an FM radio with RDS (a car radio, a kitchen radio, a phone with an FM chip)
optional: an RTL-SDR stick to see the spectrum, the RDS and the digital modes
tested: the self-test passed 36 of 36 checks on the real board (October 2026), with nothing connected; the radio service test 23 of 23.
